correctness.rationale: For n≥3 arclength-uniform iid boundary samples from a nondegenerate triangle with side proportions p_i>0, p_i<1/2, sum=1, condition on multinomial side occupancies m. Independent uniform-order statistics give expected corner missing area from each occupied side as 1/((m_j+1)(m_k+1)). Summing gives an exact trinomial expectation; integrate reciprocal counts using x^m to derive Q_n=1−[1−Σ(1−p_i)^(n+2)+Σp_i^(n+2)]/[(n+1)(n+2)∏p_i]. Triple finite difference yields 1−Q_n=n E[(Σp_i U_i)^(n−1)]. For n≥3, strict convexity under nontrivial coordinate averaging gives Schur-convex missing area, maximizing Q uniquely at p=(1/3,1/3,1/3) and minimizing Q in the limit p→(1/2,1/2,0). The fixed-p quadratic missing-area limit and triangular-degeneration nq_n→τ limit follow by exponential decay and dominated convergence. Independently checked exact multinomial expectation against formula for 21 (p,n) cases across n=3..9, including near-degenerate proportions. This is an all-n proof not an extrapolation of numerical tests.
